name: Mississippi

statute.name: Mississippi Public Records Act of 1983
statute.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 25-61-1 et seq. (response § 25-61-5; fees § 25-61-7; enforcement § 25-61-13)

response.rule_text: Public body must produce or deny within 7 working days of the request (one day if it has no written procedures); with written reasons it may take 7 additional working days, 14 total, Miss. Code Ann. § 25-61-5(1).

fees.labor_rule: Fees must be reasonably calculated to reimburse, and never exceed, the actual cost of searching, reviewing, duplicating and, if needed, mailing records (e.g. AG allowed $75/hour for building a search program).
fees.copy_rule: Actual cost of duplication; fees collected in advance, § 25-61-7.
fees.waiver_rule: No statutory provision for fee waivers.

residency.rule_text: 'Any person' may request records, Miss. Code Ann. § 25-61-5.

appeal.body: Mississippi Ethics Commission (complaint) or chancery court
appeal.rule_text: After any internal agency review, a requester may file a free complaint with the Ethics Commission (public body must respond within 14 days) or sue in chancery court of the county where the body sits, § 25-61-13; no specific time limit (general 3-year statute applies).

notes: Delay is not classified as denial by the Act (RCFP). Legislature covered but retains right to regulate access to its own records (§ 25-61-17). Appeal deadline null. Governor, universities, school districts not confirmed as coverage rules.
